question: Which subatomic particle has a negative charge but negligible mass?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Electron**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **Electron** is a subatomic particle that carries a **negative elementary electric charge**. It was the first subatomic particle to be discovered, identified by **J.J. Thomson** in **1897** during his experiments with **cathode rays**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Electron.***
 
• In terms of **mass**, an electron is extremely light, weighing approximately **9.109 x 10^-31 kilograms**. This is roughly **1/1837th** of the mass of a proton, which is why it is considered to have **negligible mass** in most atomic calculations.
 
• **Protons** are subatomic particles found in the **nucleus** of an atom with a **positive charge** of **+1** and a mass of approximately **1 atomic mass unit (amu)**. Since they have a positive charge, this option is incorrect. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
